## 2- Add extra cell_states

```{r}
## add the KC states for KCs
selected_study_cells-> selected_obj
#> get the cluster number "as character"
cluster_number = names(table(selected_obj$cell_type_0.7))
cluster_number = cluster_number[1:14]
    ##>  [1] "BAS-I"   "BAS-II"  "BAS-III" "BAS-IV"  "BAS-V"   "Fib"     "GRN-I"   "GRN-II"  "GRN-III" "MEL"    
    ## [11] "SPN-I"   "SPN-II"  "SPN-III" "SPN-IV" 

  #> make corresponding cluster annotation.
annotation_cluster = c(
"BAS",
"BAS",
"BAS",
"BAS",
"BAS",
"Fib",
"GRN",
"GRN",
"GRN",
"MEL",
"SPN",
"SPN",
"SPN",
"SPN")

# make the corresponding annotation table with cell_cluster
cluster_anno = data.frame(cluster_number, annotation_cluster, stringsAsFactors = F)

# add empty column for meta.data
selected_obj@meta.data$Cell_states = "NA"

# fill the cell types by cluster number comparison
for(i in 1:nrow(cluster_anno)) { 
selected_obj@meta.data[which(selected_obj@meta.data$cell_type_0.7 == cluster_anno$cluster_number[i]),'Cell_states'] <- cluster_anno$annotation_cluster[i] 
  }

#> check the result and performance
table(selected_obj$Cell_states)
    #  BAS  Fib  GRN  MEL  SPN 
    # 7977  451 4573  987 8487 
```

## 4- DEGs for cell states

### 4.1- Fib_HSE top10 marker genes

```{r}
## based on "Cell_states"-> BAS/FIB/GRN/SPN
DefaultAssay(Fib_obj) <- "RNA"
Idents(Fib_obj)="Cell_states"

markers_celltype <- FindAllMarkers(Fib_obj, 
                                   only.pos = TRUE, 
                                   min.pct = 0.25, 
                                   logfc.threshold = 0.25,
                                   test.use = "wilcox")

## extract top10 genes
markers_celltype %>%group_by(cluster) %>%top_n(n = 10, wt = avg_log2FC) -> top10_marker_genes_FibHSE

## save it in list() for eahc cluster,create a list where each element is a vector of genes for each cluster
top10_marker_list_FibHSE <- split(top10_marker_genes_FibHSE$gene, top10_marker_genes_FibHSE$cluster)
```

```{r}
## plot

# scale the data
all.genes <- rownames(Fib_obj)
Fib_obj <- ScaleData(Fib_obj, 
                     features = all.genes)

top10<- top10_marker_genes_FibHSE$gene

p1<-DoHeatmap(Fib_obj, 
          features = top10) + 
          NoLegend() +
  scale_fill_gradientn(colors = c("#377EB8", "white", "#E41A1C"))
#> Scale for fill is already present.
#> Adding another scale for fill, which will replace the existing scale.
#> 
#> 
ggsave(p1,filename = "R11_4.1_top10_heatmap_FibHSE.pdf",
       width = 10, height =10)
```

## 5- Load exFINDER database

```{r}
# load exFINDER database
load("exFinder_data/LR_layer1_human.rda")
load("exFinder_data/RTF_layer2_human.rda")
load("exFinder_data/TFT_layer3_human.rda")

exFINDER.H <- list()
exFINDER.H[[1]] <- LR_layer1_human
exFINDER.H[[2]] <- RTF_layer2_human
exFINDER.H[[3]] <- TFT_layer3_human
```

## 6- Prepare the inputs for exFINDER analysis

### 6.1- FibHSE

-   for external signal,

    -   Fib-only

    -   or environment, or unknown cells [not present from all cells]

```{r}
Fib_obj$Type <- as.factor(Fib_obj$Cell_states) # add "Type", very improtant for later analysis

#> [Fib-only] dataset of Fib-only cells for intersted ligand-expressing cells
cell_id <- subset(Fib_obj@meta.data, 
                  Cell_states %in% c("Fib")) # 451 cells
fib_only_cells <- subset(Fib_obj, cells=row.names(cell_id))

exp.data <- fib_only_cells@assays$RNA@data
meta.data <- fib_only_cells@meta.data ## need column ""Type" for cell labels

##> [KC-only] dataset
cell_id <- subset(Fib_obj@meta.data, 
                  !Cell_states %in% c("Fib")) # 1796 cells
kc_only_cells <- subset(Fib_obj, cells=row.names(cell_id))

exp.data2 <- kc_only_cells@assays$RNA@data
meta.data2 <- kc_only_cells@meta.data ## need column ""Type" for cell labels

#> [All cells] the complete dataset contains all cells, which used for "external signals" from unknown cells or environment.
exp.Exdata <- Fib_obj@assays$RNA@data
meta.Exdata <- Fib_obj@meta.data
```

-   check the threshold for low and high expressed genes

```{r}
## calculate the percentile values of cell groups for determining the cutoff thresholds for “barely expressed genes” and “highly expressed genes” in later analysis
data <- get_percentile(Exp.Data = exp.Exdata,
               Meta.Data = meta.Exdata,
               percentile = c(.5, .75, .90))

p1<-ggplot(data=data, aes(x=Type, 
                      y=Ave.Exp., 
                      color=Prob.)) +
  geom_point(size=3) +
  theme_bw() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 0.5, vjust = 0.5))

##
ggsave(p1,filename = "R11_6.1_threshold_check_FibHSE.pdf",
       width = 5, height =4)

## lowly expressed threshold is lower than 0.5
## highly expressed threshold is higher than 0.9 for each cell group.
## Next, we mark those lowly expressed ligands among all cell groups as potential external signals.
```

## 7- **Identify external signals that come from NON-KC cells targeting KC cells**

-   Could be the ligands from Fib or MEL.

-   ligand--target Gene Regulatory Network (GRN) = ltGRN

-   the external signal-target signaling network = (exSigNet)

### 7.1 FibHSE

-   KC is target cells, need KC marker geens.

```{r}
##> Setup target genes (From KC) and infer ltGRN
##> using KC marker genes
target.gene <- c(top10_marker_list_FibHSE$BAS,
                 top10_marker_list_FibHSE$GRN,
                 top10_marker_list_FibHSE$SPN)

##> infer ltGRN, using KC as target cells
ltGRN <- get_ltGRN(Target = target.gene, DB = exFINDER.H)
  # we get all KC-relatd itGRNs now, as ref.
```

### [All external Ligands from Fib and env, KC as targets]

-   Find all ligands not expressed from KC.

```{r}
##> Identify external signals and infer exSigNet
##> [KC-only] used here. We are intersted in the ligands of Non-KC cells, here could be only Fib.
  # should very low in KC, may be highly expressed in the Fib cells or external environment
  # based on ltGRN to find out the ligands very low in KC
  # the threshold to degine the low expressed in KC is < 0.072

meta.data2$Type <- as.factor(meta.data2$Cell_states) # ## very important
      # must be "factor" for all cell types.
Pex <- get_potentialex(Graph = ltGRN,
                Exp.Data = exp.data2,
                Meta.Data = meta.data2,
                cutoff = -0.072,
                AG.L = NULL)
## we found 643 ligands not expressed in KC
head(Pex)
#> [1] "PLEKHO2" "INHBE"   "ITGAM"   "ITGA4"   "ITGA9"   "JAM3"   

```

-   We have KC-ltGRN, and external Ligands, next, check the R/TF and target genes on Target cells t infer exSigNet. define the high threshold....

```{r}
# [KC-only] infer exSigNet (R, TF, T are all highly expressed, L comes from the potential external signals)
##> We need the Lignad low [KC], R/TF/Target high in KC.
##> 
exSigNet <- get_exSigNet(Graph = ltGRN,
                       Ligands = Pex, # the ligands must be potential external signals
                       Exp.Data = exp.data2,
                       Meta.Data = meta.data2,
                       par.cutoff = c(0.6, 0.6), #  two threshold for Receptor and TF.
                       # we select the receptors that are highly expressed in the KC
                       AG.R = c("BAS"),  
                       # we select the receptors that are highly expressed in the KC
                       AG.TF = c('BAS',"SPN","GRN"))

get_NetworkDetail(exSigNet) # show the details of exSigNet
  # Number of ligands:  132 
  # Number of receptors:  26 
  # Number of tfs:  74 
  # Number of targets:  30 
  # Number of L-R pairs:  230 
  # Number of R-TF pairs:  278 
  # Number of TF-T pairs:  497 
```

-   Check the ligand expression in all cells, KC should be very low

```{r}
# [All-cells] check the inferred external signals and their expressions via heatmap
exS <- exSigNet$Graph.Node$Gene[exSigNet$Graph.Node$Role == "Ligand"]

p1<-get_heatmap(Gene = exS,
            Exp.Data = exp.Exdata,
            Meta.Data = meta.Exdata,
            cellwidth = 20,
            cellheight = 10,
            fontsize_row = 5,
             cluster_rows = TRUE)

ggsave(p1,filename = "R11_7.1_heatmap_ligand_check_FibHSE.pdf",
       width = 10, height =20)
```

![](images/Screenshot%202025-04-08%20at%204.32.17%E2%80%AFAM.png)

### [exSigNet from Fib]

-   Identify the exSigNet from Fib

-   using the highly expressed gene thresholds

```{r}
# select the external signals that expressed by Fib cells and infer the corresponding exSigNet
exSigNet <- get_exSigNetExData(Graph = exSigNet,
                                 Exp.ExData = exp.Exdata,
                                 Meta.ExData = meta.Exdata,
                                 cutoff.ExData = 0.6,
                                 # find the external signals that are highly expressed in the Fib
                                 AG.ExData = c('Fib')) # define which Cell ligands you want to see. 
## 
## Warning: Overlap found!

#####>>>>>>>>>>>>>>.>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
## if overlap found, we shoud fix it by.

# What does “overlap” mean in this context?
# In an external signaling network (exSigNet), you usually have a directed graph showing signaling from source nodes (e.g., ligands or upstream regulators) to target nodes (e.g., DEGs or downstream transcription factors).

exSigNet <- fix_OverLap(exSigNet)
# #> [1] "No overlap found!"
```

-   calculate expression levels of the genes(nodes) in Fib, and predict signaling strength(weight).

```{r}
# calculate the expression levels in Fib, WE ARE intersted only in KC, so still use KC data for target.
exSigNet <- get_NodeValue(Graph = exSigNet,
                          Exp.Data = exp.data2, ## target cell KC
                          Meta.Data = meta.data2, ## target cell KC
                          AG.R = c("BAS"),
                          AG.TF = c('BAS',"SPN","GRN"), #
                          AG.T = c('BAS',"SPN","GRN"), # Target genes
                          Exp.ExData = exp.Exdata,
                          Meta.ExData = meta.Exdata,
                          # the expression of external signals are calculated using the data of Fib
                          AG.ExData = c('Fib'))

# predict signaling strengths (the default value of Kh is 2)
exSigNet <- get_EdgeWeight(Graph = exSigNet, 
               Kh = 2)
```

### [Visualize for Fib ligands] exSigNet heatmap

```{r}
# prepare the dataframe for heatmap plot [Fib ligand-target network]
exS_exp <- get_AveExp(Gene = unique(exSigNet$Graph.Node$Gene),
           Exp.Data = exp.Exdata, # all cells
           Meta.Data = meta.Exdata)  # all cells

exS_exp.HP <- exS_exp
exS_exp.HP <- exS_exp.HP[, -1]
row.names(exS_exp.HP) <- exS_exp$Gene

# make data.frame includes all cell states
exS_exp.HP <- data.frame("BAS" = exS_exp.HP$BAS,
                     "SPN" = exS_exp.HP$SPN, 
                     'GRN' = exS_exp.HP$GRN,
                     "Fib" = exS_exp.HP$Fib)

row.names(exS_exp.HP) <- exS_exp$Gene

# [annotation col] customize the row labels and col labels
annotation_col = data.frame(
  CellType = c("KC", "KC", "KC", "Fibroblasts"))
rownames(annotation_col) = colnames(exS_exp.HP)


# [annotation row] remove the duplicate
table_2 <- data.frame(Role = exSigNet$Graph.Node$Role,
                      Gene= exSigNet$Graph.Node$Gene )
    # ‘CAV1’, ‘EGFR’, ‘ITGA6’

library(openxlsx) # outpt for modify
write.xlsx(table_2,rowNames=F,
           "table_2.xlsx") 
library(readxl) # input for using
s1 <- read_excel("table_2.xlsx")

## ready for plot
annotation_row <- data.frame(Role = s1$Role)
rownames(annotation_row) <- s1$Gene
```

### **[Visualize for Fib ligands] exSigNet hierarchy plot**

```{r}
## If get_readyforplot is erro, says "Error in data.frame(name = unique(c(as.character(hierarchy$from), as.character(hierarchy$to))),  : arguments imply differing number of rows: 102, 105"
## think about remove the duplicated rows for gene columns, don't remove them, keep at least one, if not ,will keep error for plotting.

#>> Get genes that appear more than once
exSigNet$Graph.Node-> aa 
duplicated_genes <- aa$Gene[duplicated(aa$Gene) | duplicated(aa$Gene, fromLast = TRUE)]
  # Get unique duplicated gene names
duplicated_genes_unique <- unique(duplicated_genes)
      ## "ITGA6" [as receptor] "CAV1" [keep as receptor];  "EGFR" [as recepotr]

#>> Now you know which genes are duplicates in Gene columnm next need export them and remove them keep unique one, manually.
  library(openxlsx) ## export
  write.xlsx(aa,rowNames=F,
           "aa.xlsx") 
#>> input again to replace original exSigNet
  # exSigNet-> backup, in case
  library(readxl) # input for using
  s1 <- read_excel("aa.xlsx")

# replace old by new one.
exSigNet$Graph.Node <- s1

#>>>>  hierarchy plot
# after remove the duplicates in "gene" column in exSigNet$Graph.Node, error disappeared.
exSigNet_plot <- get_readyforplot(Graph = exSigNet)
```

```{r}
p <- ggraph(exSigNet_plot[[1]], layout = 'dendrogram', circular = TRUE) + 
  geom_node_point(aes(filter = leaf, x=x, y=y, colour=Role, size=Expression)) +
  theme_void() +
  geom_conn_bundle(data = get_con(from = exSigNet_plot[[2]]$from, 
                                  to = exSigNet_plot[[2]]$to, 
                                  Strength = exSigNet_plot[[2]]$weight), 
                   width = 1.0, aes(colour=Strength), 
                   arrow = arrow(length = unit(3, 'mm')), start_cap = circle(3, 'mm'), end_cap = circle(3, 'mm')) +

ggsave(p,filename = "R11_7.1_hiplot_exSigNet_for_Fib_FibHSE.pdf",
       width = 12, height =10)

# there are too many interaction from Fib.

##> first filtert the edges Weight [define the threshold is ok]
if (F) {exSigNet-> Graph
edges <- data.frame("from" = Graph$Graph.Edge$from, "to" = Graph$Graph.Edge$to)
edges <- edges %>%
  mutate(weight = Graph$Graph.Edge$Weight)
}
## once you have the edges genes list, keep them, to filter the exSigNet$Graph.Node
```

## 8- Identify external signals come from absent cells or env targeting KC cells.

-   *come from external environment* means very low (or zero) expressions in all measured cells (Fib and KC cells).

```{r}
##> Setup target genes (From KC) and infer ltGRN
##> using KC marker genes
target.gene <- c(top10_marker_list_FibHSE$BAS,
                 top10_marker_list_FibHSE$GRN,
                 top10_marker_list_FibHSE$SPN)

##> infer ltGRN, using KC as target cells
ltGRN.2 <- get_ltGRN(Target = target.gene, DB = exFINDER.H)
  # we get all KC-relatd itGRNs now, as ref.
```

### 8.1 FibHSE

### [All external Ligands from env, KC as targets]

```{r}
# infer potential external signals from ltGRN: low expression in measured cells [All cells], here predict only ligands
Pex.2 <- get_potentialex(Graph = ltGRN.2,
                Exp.Data = exp.Exdata,
                Meta.Data = meta.Exdata,
                cutoff = -0.05, # lower threshold
                AG.L = NULL) # all from env ligand
head(Pex.2)
#> [1] "INHBE" "ITGAM" "ITGA4" "ITGA9" "JAM2"  "L1CAM"
```

-   the KC-related exSigNet from env.

```{r}
# [KC-only] infer exSigNet (R, TF, T are all highly expressed, L comes from the potential external signals)
##> We need the Lignad low [KC], R/TF/Target high in KC.
##> 
exSigNet.2 <- get_exSigNet(Graph = ltGRN.2,
                       Ligands = Pex.2, # the ligands must be potential external signals
                       Exp.Data = exp.data2,
                       Meta.Data = meta.data2,
                       par.cutoff = c(0.6, 0.6), #  two threshold for Receptor and TF.
                       # we select the receptors that are highly expressed in the KC
                       AG.R = c("BAS"),  
                       # we select the receptors that are highly expressed in the KC
                       AG.TF = c('BAS',"SPN","GRN"))

get_NetworkDetail(exSigNet.2) # show the details of exSigNet
  # Number of ligands:  85 
  # Number of receptors:  24 
  # Number of tfs:  73 
  # Number of targets:  30 
  # Number of L-R pairs:  143 
  # Number of R-TF pairs:  250 
  # Number of TF-T pairs:  496
```

### **[Visualize for env ligand] exSigNet via hive plot**

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(igraph)

## preapre for plot 
Graph <- exSigNet.2

Role <- factor(x = Graph$Graph.Node$Role, levels = c("Ligand", "Receptor", "TF", "Target"))

edges <- data.frame("from" = Graph$Graph.Edge$from, "to" = Graph$Graph.Edge$to)

edges <- edges %>%
  mutate(weight = Graph$Graph.Edge$Weight)

nodes <- data.frame(name = Graph$Graph.Node$Gene, role = Role, value = Graph$Graph.Node$Size)

g2 <- graph_from_data_frame(vertices = nodes, d = edges)
```

```{r}
p<- ggraph(g2, 'hive', axis = nodes$role) + 
  geom_edge_hive(aes(colour = weight), width = 0.7, 
                 arrow = arrow(length = unit(3, 'mm')), 
                 start_cap = circle(3, 'mm'), 
                 end_cap = circle(3, 'mm')) + 
  # geom_axis_hive(aes(colour = role), size = 0, label = FALSE) + 
  geom_node_point(aes(size = value, color = role),  alpha = 1) +
  geom_node_text(aes(label = name), angle = 45,  size = 6, repel = TRUE) +
  coord_fixed() +
  scale_edge_color_continuous(low="#80b1d3", high="#FF7F24") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    axis.line = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks =element_blank(),
    axis.text =element_blank(),
    axis.title = element_blank()
  ) 

# save
ggsave(p,filename = "R11_8.1_hive_plot_exSigNet_for_env_FibHSE.pdf",
       width = 12, height =10)
```

```{r}
library(igraph)
library(RColorBrewer)

Graph <- exSigNet.TF

# assigne the target cell colors
Graph$Graph.Node$Role[Graph$Graph.Node$Gene %in% c("KRT16", "KRT14")] = "Target (SPN+GRN)" # define the color for target 1
Graph$Graph.Node$Role[Graph$Graph.Node$Gene %in% c("S100A2")] = "Target (BAS)" # define the color for target 2

actors <- data.frame(
  name = Graph$Graph.Node$Gene,
  role = Graph$Graph.Node$Role
)

relations <- data.frame(
  from = Graph$Graph.Edge$from,
  to = Graph$Graph.Edge$to
)

g <- graph_from_data_frame(
  relations, directed = TRUE,
  vertices = actors
)

l <- layout_with_gem(g) 

coul  <- brewer.pal(5, "Set2") 
# Create a vector of color
my_color <- coul[as.numeric(as.factor(V(g)$role))]

# save
pdf("R11_9.1_topo_TF_exSigNet_for_env_FibHSE.pdf")
plot(g, layout=l, vertex.color=my_color)
```
